title.it: Da tanto tempo: I've been waiting
title.en: I've been waiting for an hour

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj traja do zdaj (I've been waiting for an hour), ločiš dejavnost od rezultata (She's been baking, She's baked forty scones) in veš, kateri glagoli ostanejo brez -ing.
goal.de: Du sagst, was bis jetzt andauert (I've been waiting for an hour), trennst Tätigkeit und Ergebnis (She's been baking, She's baked forty scones) und weißt, welche Verben ohne -ing bleiben.
goal.it: Dici ciò che dura fino a ora (I've been waiting for an hour), distingui l'attività dal risultato (She's been baking, She's baked forty scones) e sai quali verbi restano senza -ing.
goal.en: You can say what has gone on up to now (I've been waiting for an hour), tell the activity from the result (She's been baking, She's baked forty scones), and know which verbs stay without -ing.

say.sl: **I've been waiting for an hour**: **have**, **has** + **been** + -ing za to, kar traja do zdaj. (Čakam že eno uro.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Od ponedeljka dežuje.) Slovenščina reče sedanjik in *že*. Na Irskem rečejo tudi *I'm waiting for an hour*, nekateri *I been waiting*; v pisanju je **I've been waiting**.
say.de: **I've been waiting for an hour**: **have**, **has** + **been** + -ing für das, was bis jetzt andauert. (Ich warte seit einer Stunde.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Seit Montag regnet es.) Deutsch sagt Präsens und *seit*. In Irland sagt man auch *I'm waiting for an hour*, manche *I been waiting*; geschrieben steht **I've been waiting**.
say.it: **I've been waiting for an hour**: **have**, **has** + **been** + -ing per ciò che dura fino a ora. (Aspetto da un'ora.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Piove da lunedì.) L'italiano dice il presente e *da*. In Irlanda si dice anche *I'm waiting for an hour*, qualcuno *I been waiting*; per iscritto **I've been waiting**.
say.en: **I've been waiting for an hour**: **have**, **has** + **been** + -ing for what has been going on up to now. **It's been raining since Monday.** In Ireland people also say *I'm waiting for an hour*, and some people *I been waiting*; writing wants **I've been waiting**.

Jack has been walking since six.
examples.de: Jack ist seit sechs Uhr zu Fuß unterwegs.

say.de: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?** Es sagt auch, was gerade aufgehört hat und was man noch sieht. (Du bist nass. Warst du schwimmen?) **It's been raining: the road's wet.** (Es hat geregnet: Die Straße ist nass.) **Your hands are black. — I've been mending the van.**
say.it: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?** Dice anche ciò che è appena finito e che si vede ancora. (Sei bagnat{m:o|f:a}. Hai nuotato?) **It's been raining: the road's wet.** (Ha piovuto: la strada è bagnata.) **Your hands are black. — I've been mending the van.**
say.en: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?** It also tells what has just stopped and you can still see. **It's been raining: the road's wet.** **Your hands are black. — I've been mending the van.**

ask.prompt: You're out of breath. Have you been ___?

say.sl: **I've been painting the gate** pove čas in dejavnost: morda še ni končano. **I've painted the gate** pove rezultat: končano je. Koliko časa: **She's been baking all morning.** (Vse dopoldne peče.) Koliko česa: **She's baked forty scones.** (Spekla je štirideset sconesov.)
say.de: **I've been painting the gate** sagt die Zeit und die Tätigkeit: vielleicht nicht fertig. **I've painted the gate** sagt das Ergebnis: Es ist fertig. Wie lange: **She's been baking all morning.** (Sie bäckt den ganzen Vormittag.) Wie viel: **She's baked forty scones.** (Sie hat vierzig Scones gebacken.)
say.it: **I've been painting the gate** dice il tempo e l'attività: forse non è finito. **I've painted the gate** dice il risultato: è finito. Quanto tempo: **She's been baking all morning.** (Inforna da tutta la mattina.) Quanti: **She's baked forty scones.** (Ha sfornato quaranta scone.)
say.en: **I've been painting the gate** tells the time and the activity: perhaps it isn't finished. **I've painted the gate** tells the result: it's done. How long: **She's been baking all morning.** How many: **She's baked forty scones.**

examples.de: Ich war dabei, das Tor zu streichen.
examples.it: Ho pitturato il cancello, non ho ancora finito.

say.sl: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe** povedo, kako je, zato ostanejo brez -ing. Tudi **be** in **have** za to, kar imaš. **I've known Jack for years.** (Jacka poznam že leta.) **I've had this van since 2015.** (Ta kombi imam od leta 2015.) Dejavnost pa -ing dobi: **We've been having breakfast.**
say.de: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe** sagen, wie etwas ist, darum bleiben sie ohne -ing. Ebenso **be** und **have** für Besitz. **I've known Jack for years.** (Ich kenne Jack seit Jahren.) **I've had this van since 2015.** (Diesen Lieferwagen habe ich seit 2015.) Eine Tätigkeit bekommt -ing: **We've been having breakfast.**
say.it: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe** dicono come stanno le cose, perciò restano senza -ing. Così anche **be** e **have** per ciò che possiedi. **I've known Jack for years.** (Conosco Jack da anni.) **I've had this van since 2015.** (Ho questo furgone dal 2015.) Un'attività prende -ing: **We've been having breakfast.**
say.en: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe** say how things are, so they stay without -ing. So do **be** and **have** for what you own. **I've known Jack for years.** **I've had this van since 2015.** An activity takes -ing: **We've been having breakfast.**

say.sl: **I've lived here for ten years** in **I've been living here for ten years**: pri **live**, **work**, **stay**, **wait** je oboje prav. Z -ing zveni bolj za nekaj časa: **I've been staying at the inn since Monday.** (Od ponedeljka sem v gostilni.)
say.de: **I've lived here for ten years** und **I've been living here for ten years**: Bei **live**, **work**, **stay**, **wait** geht beides. Mit -ing klingt es eher vorübergehend: **I've been staying at the inn since Monday.** (Ich wohne seit Montag im Gasthaus.)
say.it: **I've lived here for ten years** e **I've been living here for ten years**: con **live**, **work**, **stay**, **wait** vanno bene tutti e due. Con -ing suona più temporaneo: **I've been staying at the inn since Monday.** (Alloggio alla locanda da lunedì.)
say.en: **I've lived here for ten years** and **I've been living here for ten years**: with **live**, **work**, **stay**, **wait**, both are right. With -ing it sounds more for a while: **I've been staying at the inn since Monday.**

exercises.text: — You look cold, love. How long have you ___ (wait)? — I've been waiting ___ an hour! — The Keswick bus? It's ___ (run) late all week. What have you been ___ (do) today? — I've been ___ (help) Sam. We've ___ (clean) the whole van, and it's finished. — You've got paint on your hands! — Yes, I've been ___ (paint) Mr Dixon's gate.

translation.sl: — Zdi se, da te zebe. Koliko časa že čakaš? — Čakam že eno uro! — Avtobus za Keswick? Ves teden zamuja. Kaj si danes počel{m:|f:a}? — Pomagal{m:|f:a} sem Samu. Očistili smo ves kombi in je končano. — Barvo imaš na rokah! — Ja, barval{m:|f:a} sem vrata gospoda Dixona.
translation.de: — Dir ist kalt, oder? Wie lange wartest du schon? — Ich warte seit einer Stunde! — Der Bus nach Keswick? Er hat die ganze Woche Verspätung. Was hast du heute gemacht? — Ich habe Sam geholfen. Wir haben den ganzen Lieferwagen geputzt, und er ist fertig. — Du hast Farbe an den Händen! — Ja, ich habe das Tor von Mr Dixon gestrichen.
translation.it: — Sembra che tu abbia freddo. Da quanto tempo aspetti? — Aspetto da un'ora! — L'autobus per Keswick? È in ritardo da tutta la settimana. Che cosa hai fatto oggi? — Ho aiutato Sam. Abbiamo pulito tutto il furgone, ed è finito. — Hai la vernice sulle mani! — Sì, ho pitturato il cancello di Mr Dixon.
translation.en: — You look cold, love. How long have you been waiting? — I've been waiting for an hour! — The Keswick bus? It's been running late all week. What have you been doing today? — I've been helping Sam. We've cleaned the whole van, and it's finished. — You've got paint on your hands! — Yes, I've been painting Mr Dixon's gate.

translation.sl: Od ponedeljka dežuje in potok je visok. Gospod Dixon ves dan dela na dežju. Poznam ga že leta. Danes je popravil dvoje vrat in so končana. — Si {m:zadihan|f:zadihana}! Si {m:tekel|f:tekla}?
translation.de: Seit Montag regnet es, und der Bach ist hoch. Mr Dixon arbeitet den ganzen Tag im Regen. Ich kenne ihn seit Jahren. Er hat heute zwei Tore repariert, und sie sind fertig. — Du bist außer Atem! Bist du gelaufen?
translation.it: Piove da lunedì e il ruscello è alto. Mr Dixon lavora sotto la pioggia da tutto il giorno. Lo conosco da anni. Oggi ha riparato due cancelli, e sono finiti. — Hai il fiatone! Hai corso?
translation.en: It has been raining since Monday, and the beck is high. Mr Dixon has been working in the rain all day. I've known him for years. He's mended two gates today, and they're finished. — You're out of breath! Have you been running?
